scope: FTQ/ResolveQueue/CommitQueue strict input domains, immutable metadata, atomic writes and claim rejection; partial adaptation, not completion of the three DUTs

red.failure: CallRet accepted lossy/out-of-domain values and unvalidated objects; the complete legal domain control passed
Scalar bool/float coercion, caller-owned mutable Meta.fields and partial valid writes on late field rejection; legal full-width group passed
A rejected group leaked its earlier free-pin claim; duplicate logical input aliases were accepted; disjoint equal labels remained legal
Second owner of the same physical input was accepted when its label equalled the first driver's label

implementation: CallRet rejects anything other than exact6-bit pointer and2-bit integer RAS action; all256 combinations remain legal. CommitQueue and FTQ encoders reject unvalidated duck-typed payloads. submit validates before mutating the FIFO oracle or starting a driver.
Prediction pointers, Meta/redirect identities, resolve fields and consumer controls reject implicit bool/float coercion. Meta.fields copies the caller's mapping and exposes a read-only snapshot.
Pins.set validates every key, input direction, exact integer and actual width before any Set. Late unknown field or overflow cannot leave valid asserted.

Dut.claim_many validates a whole claim first. Equal component labels do not excuse a second physical owner; duplicate aliases and conflict do not leave partial new claims. This is still a registry, not SDK Driver or complete runtime lifetime certification.

physical_schema_audit.address_boundary: Existing ResolveReport pc/target values are49-bit halfword Pc.addr coordinates; BPU prediction startPc uses50-bit GuardedPc.addr. Backend/IFU redirect pc/target are full byte-address UInts. Current input numbers are preserved, not implicitly re-scaled. Resolve's50th raw bit is now rejected instead of silently truncated.
physical_schema_audit.limit: This field check is not independent certification of every generated width, producer reachability or complete FTQ epoch/age semantics. Those remain required.
